title: Plan
description: A plan as a topology plus approximate dimensions — enough to check, not enough to build. Deliberately hand-authorable: you should be able to type a sketch into this in five minutes and find out whether the rules are right. It is also the natural export target for a CAD reader later, and the natural output of a composer.

style.description: style node id. Drives which exceptions apply, which constraints are checked, and which kit resolves.

massing.description: massing id, where the plan is meant to sit in a known skeleton.

groupings.description: Groupings the plan claims to contain. Declaring one asks the validator to check its internal rules.

jurisdiction.description: Code checks are advisory and jurisdictional; naming this makes the caveat explicit.

date_of_representation.description: Which year within the style's span the design represents. Sash pattern, hardware and fanlights are all date-conditional.

index.description: 0 ground, 1 first above, -1 cellar. Used for stacking checks.

type.description: room id from the room catalogue

width_ft.description: The SHORT dimension. Most room rules key off it.

window_head_ft.description: Head height above finished floor. With room depth this decides whether the far end of the room is lit.

exterior_walls.description: Which walls are on the outside. Counted against the room type's sides_lit requirement.

doors.description: Doors imply a direct-door adjacency in both directions; the validator derives the graph from them.

fixtures.description: Plumbing and equipment present — wc, lavatory, tub, shower, sink, dishwasher, washer, water-heater, furnace. Drives the servicing checks.

stacks_over.description: room id on the level below, for plumbing and structure.

site.description: Lot and settlement data beyond what `context` already carries. `context.lot_width_ft`/`lot_depth_ft`/`entrance_faces` stay where they were first established (WP-0.1) and are already load-bearing across the reference corpus and the composer; this object holds the fields WP-2.4 added so the composer can honour lot width, site-scope constraints (the Charleston piazza bearing, a bank house's cross-slope) can evaluate, and the renderer can draw the lot. A plan or brief with no site data omits this object entirely — nothing requires it.

street_bearing_deg.description: Compass bearing (0 = north, clockwise) of the street the principal front faces.

slope_direction_deg.description: Compass bearing of the downhill direction across the lot. Distinct from cross_slope_pct, which is the slope's magnitude.

cross_slope_pct.description: Cross-slope of the site across the building's depth, as a percentage -- what a bank house's plan type depends on existing at all.

prevailing_summer_wind_deg.description: Compass bearing the prevailing summer wind blows FROM.

piazza_bearing_deg.description: Compass bearing a piazza, porch, loggia or gallery faces, for a style that ties that orientation to sun or wind -- the Charleston single house's canonical use.

adjacencies.description: Relationships the doors do not express — a shared wall, a sight line, an acoustic separation.

measurements.description: Any additional numbers for the fault corpus to test — elevation dimensions, trim sizes, ratios. Keys must match the fault corpus vocabulary; see tdl_measurement_vocabulary.

declared.description: Design choices the plan asserts, keyed by element slot id, for checking against the style's forbidden variants. e.g. {"roof_form": "gambrel", "shutter": "none"}.

provenance.description: Where this record came from and how much to trust it — the structured provenance WP-2.1 asked for after carrying source_image, confidence and the style reasoning as prose in `note`. Optional: an authored record needs none; an ingested one (traced from a drawing, imported from a drafter's DXF) should say so. Added in 0.2.0 (WP-5.5).

source.description: The drawing, image file, HABS sheet or DXF this record was produced from.

method.description: authored: written directly against the schema. traced: transcribed by tracing a drawing (the WP-5.5 form). dxf-import: extracted from a drafter's DXF and completed by a human. multimodal-reading: read off an image by a model (the WP-2.1 batch).

transcription_confidence.description: Overall confidence of the transcription. Where it varies by field, use field_confidence as well.

field_confidence.description: Per-field confidence where it differs from the overall call, keyed by a dotted field path (e.g. "levels.0.rooms.kitchen.windows").

style_reasoning.description: Why the style id was chosen — a traced record's style is a judgment; the reasoning rides with it, never silently.

traced_by.description: Who or what performed the transcription.
